name: PHOSPHORUS
description: Phosphorus (phosphate) measurement evaluates inorganic phosphorus levels in serum using colorimetric methods. Phosphorus is essential for bone mineralization, energy metabolism, and acid-base balance. Abnormal levels can indicate kidney disease, parathyroid disorders, and metabolic bone diseases.

testdeatils.instrumentation: Roche Cobas, Beckman Coulter, Abbott Architect

literatureReview: Phosphorus (phosphate) is essential for bone structure, energy storage (ATP), and cellular signaling. Serum phosphorus measurement uses colorimetric methods based on phosphomolybdate complex formation. Normal adult range is 2.5-4.5 mg/dL, with variations by age and sex. Hypophosphatemia (<2.5 mg/dL) occurs in malnutrition, vitamin D deficiency, hyperparathyroidism, and refeeding syndrome. Hyperphosphatemia (>4.5 mg/dL) is common in chronic kidney disease, hypoparathyroidism, and tumor lysis syndrome. Phosphorus homeostasis involves parathyroid hormone, vitamin D, and FGF-23. Levels fluctuate with meals, so fasting samples are preferred. Results should be interpreted with calcium, PTH, and vitamin D levels. Hemolysis can falsely elevate phosphorus due to red cell content.
